newsitem.title: UK: Dollar soft in late Europe amid keen yen appetite.
newsitem.headline: Dollar soft in late Europe amid keen yen appetite.

text.p: Dollar/yen drifted down throughout the European afternoon, unsettling dollar/mark, as the yen climbed on crosses amid nerves about Japanese economic strength.
Traders said the yen attracted particular demand against the Swiss franc and the mark, and that helped drag the dollar below the psychological 111 yen prop.

In a market hypersensitive to interest rate moves, sterling powered to fresh four-year highs against the dollar as speculation bubbled of monetary tightening. But the day's rash of U.S. data was mixed and ambivalent, shedding little light on the near-term prospects for U.S. rates, analysts said.

U.S. October industrial production showed a surprise 0.5 percent drop, confounding expectations of a 0.2 rise, after September's 0.3 growth. Analysts said the General Motors strike hit manufacturing and the dip should be short-lived.
Capacity utilization came in at 82.7, below the expected 83.0 and September's 83.4, while September business inventories rose 0.1 percent compared to the predicted 0.2.
But the University of Michigan sentiment survey for November outstripped forecasts with a rise to 98.9 from October's 96.5.
"You need something a lot more conclusive to move the market," said Adrian Schmidt, international economist at Chase.
"There's so much mixed data coming out that I don't think anyone's prepared to take a strong view on the U.S. economy at this stage," he said.
The dollar slipped to lows of 110.65 yen and 1.5046 marks intraday before recovering to 111.10/15 and 1.5084/89 by 1611 GMT. It ended at 111.27/32 and 1.5103/08 in Europe on Thursday.
Mark/yen was off a 73.57 session low at 73.65/68 and Swiss/yen was above a low of 86.75, its worst level since June.
"There's a lot going on in Swiss/yen, that seems to be the big move. The Swissie's very, very weak," said Pat Magill, head of the corporate desk at Daiwa Europe in London.
The Swiss franc took a tumble against the mark, falling to a 20-month low of 84.77 centimes during the European session.
Japanese trade data for October are due at 2350 GMT, and are expected to show the surplus declining at a slower pace -- or even rising for the first time in 23 months.
That kind of speculation helped boost the yen today, analysts said. The focus is now turning to the Tankan report on November 26-27 for more clues to the state of Japan's economy.
The yen also continued to draw strength from unconfirmed reports that known dollar/yen bear Fred Bergsten might be offered a top economic post in the new U.S. administration.

That upset the dollar, coming as it did just as the market was regaining confidence that the G3 strong-dollar consensus was not unravelling, as feared last week after comments from influential Japanese finance official Eisuke Sakakibara.
Heavyweights from Germany, the U.S., Japan and France have lined up recently to pledge their commitment to a strong dollar.

But Klaus Baader, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell here, felt the Bundesbank's defence of the dollar had been half-hearted. "The Bundesbank is willing to talk in pursuit of a stronger dollar, but as ever refuses to take any action to back up its words," he said.
"Germany has not been an active buyer of foreign currencies to back up its calls for a stronger dollar," he added.
The mark gleaned support from Germany's five "wise men" panel of economic advisors, who predicted 2.5-percent German growth in 1997 after 1.5-percent growth in 1996.
Sterling raced ahead during the session, scoring a four-year high against the dollar, 30-month high versus the mark and pushing to its best trade-weighted level in 34 months.
The pound stood at $1.6646/56 and 2.5115/25 marks by 1652 GMT, off intraday highs of $1.6697 and 2.5180.
-- Abigail Levene, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8968
